research.title: eXpath · Explainable knowledge graph reasoning framework
research.summary: Addresses the black-box nature of embedding-model decisions by independently proposing an explanation framework that combines ontological closed-path rules and relational-path evidence.
details: Designs a structured explanation-generation mechanism that coordinates rule mining and path search, integrating ontological closed-path rules with relational-path evidence into a quantitatively evaluable framework.

On standard benchmarks, improves two explanation-quality metrics by approximately 20% and reduces explanation-generation time by 61.4% against the best comparison method, demonstrating gains in both explanation quality and computational efficiency.

research.title: RuleDep · Dependency-aware rule aggregation
research.summary: Leads the design of sparse second-order corrections and a two-stage training framework to model complementarity and redundancy in rule aggregation through dependencies among jointly triggered rules and signed gains in log-failure evidence space.
details: Across seven datasets, raises average MRR from 0.382 to 0.396, achieves 21 best or tied-best metrics among interpretable methods, and improves MRR by approximately 10.7% on dependency-rich subsets.

research.title: GeneticPrism · Hierarchical graph layout and scholarly evolution visualization
research.summary: Addresses the joint representation of within-topic citations and cross-topic influence in multi-topic scholarly evolution by proposing a hierarchical graph representation and IFHL (Integrated Flow Hierarchical Layout) layout.
details: Leads the design of the GeneticPrism overview and GeneticScroll detail views for topic overlap, temporal evolution, and cross-topic influence, enabling linked multi-scale exploration and deeper analytical insight.

research.title: INSPIRE · Expressive Piano Performance Generation
research.status: AAAI 2027, CCF-A · First author · Revision (initial review passed)
research.summary: Builds a note-level structured performance-generation framework using PyTorch and supervised fine-tuning of a Transformer (T5), generating expressive performances from discrete symbols through relative-timing modeling and continuous distribution prediction.
details: Designs typed encoding that fuses pitch, duration, dynamics, and other note attributes into a single Transformer timestep, with score-relative timing deviations for fine-grained expressive control.

On ASAP, reduces PP HR by 15.2% against PianistTransformer; architecture and inference-flow optimization reduces the reported test-task inference cost by 95.3%, improving deployability and iteration efficiency.

experience.title: National Key R&D Program: Rare-earth catalysis knowledge graph and full-process digital R&D platform
experience.summary: Led construction of the database and materials knowledge graph, participating throughout the project from proposal to acceptance and ensuring scheduled delivery reviews.
details: Designed and built a multimodal materials database at the 10^5 scale with 46,701 synthesis conditions, integrating heterogeneous data.
Applied the knowledge graph to synthesis-condition recommendation and knowledge discovery to support intelligent materials R&D workflows.

experience.title: GeneticFlow V2.0 · Large-scale scholarly literature visualization system
experience.summary: Leads development of a multidimensional visualization system for million-scale scholarly literature, integrating graph-layout computation with visual interaction; the system has served 110,419 users, supported 540,440 visits, and received software copyright registration.
details: Compiles Graphviz C++ sources into browser-side layout components, connecting graph-layout computation with front-end interaction through independent full-stack development and operations.
ACM Fellow Ion Stoica commented: "This is interesting, especially the visualization."

experience.title: Software Engineering course project: Multi-domain Intelligent Text Annotation and Mining System (ITAS)
experience.summary: Led requirements analysis, product planning, and implementation. ITAS is a multi-domain system for scientific-literature annotation and information extraction.
details: Supports batch PDF upload, paragraph and entity annotation, review, model export, and few-shot extraction with large language models.
Built a BM25 + RAG few-shot workflow that returns structured JSON for precursors, amounts, and synthesis conditions; achieved macro-F1 0.94 across three MOF datasets and 0.77 zero-shot.

experience.title: University–industry collaboration project: Research-agent-based data classification
experience.summary: Led development of LLM-based entity-recognition tools and built a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) data-classification and grading system for automated sensitive-data annotation and dynamic refinement.
details: The system has five core modules: prompt generation, model interfaces, RAG retrieval augmentation, result processing, and performance evaluation, connected through an end-to-end classify workflow.

Applied across steel production, education, and other domains; supports sample-library, classification-standard, project, task, and environment management, with more than 100,000 records in the pending-classification database.
The team was recognized among Beihang University’s Top 10 Outstanding Teams in Artificial Intelligence.
